title: MUSA device identity: pymtml reports physical ids, MUSA_VISIBLE_DEVICES remaps only torch
summary: The plugin's MTML/pymtml path answers with physical device ids and is explicitly documented as unaffected by MUSA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, while torch.musa applies logical ids. A campaign that pins cards only through MUSA_VISIBLE_DEVICES can therefore measure a different physical device than the one it names, and two arms can land on different cards.

hardware: Moore Threads MUSA GPU; the SKU and driver are not stated by the cited source
software: torch_musa plus mthreads-ml-py (pymtml); torchada is imported by the plugin
models: Any model served through the vllm-musa platform plugin
conditions: Applies whenever MUSA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is set to a subset or a reordering
The cited commit also removed a baked MUSA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all default from the image

claims.description: platform.py states that MTML is not affected by MUSA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and that its functions work on real physical device ids.
The MtmlMUSAPlatform device-capability path carries an explicit note that torch.musa uses logical ids while pymtml does not remap, so it queries the handle by the caller-supplied id.

Because only torch applies the remapping, an experiment that selects devices solely through MUSA_VISIBLE_DEVICES has no guarantee that a vendor-tool reading of card N and a torch reading of device N refer to the same physical card.

recommendations: Record the physical id, UUID and name read through pymtml for every campaign arm, not only the MUSA_VISIBLE_DEVICES string.
Prefer selecting devices by UUID when the harness supports it; otherwise pin both the physical ids and the env remapping and state the mapping in the evidence.
Before comparing arms, assert the same physical UUID set on both sides; a differing UUID set invalidates the comparison even when the env string is identical.
validation_plan: On the target host, print pymtml index/UUID/name and torch.musa device properties with and without MUSA_VISIBLE_DEVICES set, and record both.
Run one pair of arms with the identical physical UUID set and confirm the harness reports the same device identity for both.
Repeat with a reordered MUSA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to confirm the trap and to show the identity check catches it.
limitations: Source-derived reading of the plugin; it was not exercised on MUSA hardware while this record was written.
The exact remapping semantics belong to torch_musa and may change independently of the plugin.
A UUID check proves identity, not performance; it is a precondition for a valid A/B comparison only.
